rationale.usefulness: Documented performance direction, phonemes and multi-speaker controls are strongly actionable for narrated lessons and creative production (fish-drama-docs); the report proposes concrete listening and accepted-take evaluations without inventing results.
rationale.impact: Direction-aware speech and downloadable weights could materially advance an important creative domain (fish-drama3, fish-drama-card), but no independently verified quality improvement establishes field-wide exceptional impact.
rationale.novelty: Natural-language direction, word-level control and the vendor-described preference-reward shift form a meaningfully differentiated speech workflow (fish-drama-docs, fish-drama3). Experimental language switching and untested editing remain qualified.
rationale.maturity: Current website/app/API access and detailed documentation support usable evaluation; new release status, invite-only hosted editing, silent model fallback, H200-scoped measurements and no listening trial limit readiness (fish-release, fish-header, fish-card-scope).
rationale.openness: Weights and code permit inspection and local experiments, but conditional commercial revenue eligibility, separately licensed hosted services, attribution, voice consent and other-model training restrictions materially constrain portability and reuse (fish-drama-license, fish-repo).

concerns: Non-blocking retained inconsistency: the Hub metadata says research license while the inspected artifact LICENSE is Community License v1.0 dated 2026-10-13. The report appropriately relies on the actual file for its bounded description and does not certify an organization’s eligibility.

Chrome spot-check on 2026-10-18 confirmed LICENSE sections III(a)–III(c), IV(a)–IV(b), hosted-service exceptions, affiliate aggregation, the dated launch and invite-only hosted editing. Model capability versus product access is a scope difference, not a surviving contradiction.
No listening test, local execution or independent benchmark reproduction.
